model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty terms for a language model, comparing the base model (Mistralv0.2-Base, shown in light blue) against versions fine-tuned on six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics (each represented by a distinct shade of orange or brown). The vertical axis, labeled "Negative log probability," is scaled linearly from -27 to -22, with tick marks at intervals of 1. The horizontal axis, labeled "Per-specialty terms," displays the six specialties in alphabetical order. For each specialty, there are seven bars: the first (light blue) represents the base model’s performance, and the following six (in varying shades of orange/brown) represent the performance of models fine-tuned on each of the six specialties. The chart shows that for each specialty, the fine-tuned model on that specialty achieves the lowest (most negative) log probability, indicating higher likelihood or better performance, while the base model consistently performs worse (higher negative log probability) across all specialties. For example, in the "Cardio" category, the base model’s bar reaches approximately -22.3, while the fine-tuned Cardio model’s bar reaches about -26.8. Similarly, in "Pediatrics," the base model’s bar is around -22.5, and the fine-tuned Pediatrics model’s bar is approximately -26.5. The bars are grouped by specialty, with each group containing seven bars side-by-side, and the legend at the top indicates the color coding for each fine-tuned model and the base model.
